rows.question: Please generate a summary of the closing balances at the end of each month for each customer transactions, show the monthly changes and monthly cumulative bank account balances. Ensure that even if a customer has no account activity in a given month, the balance for that month is still included in the output.

WITH months AS (
  -- generate month grid from earliest txn to latest txn across all customers
  SELECT date(min_month || '-01', '+' || (n||' months')) AS month_start_date,
         CAST(strftime('%Y', date(min_month || '-01', '+' || (n||' months')) ) AS INTEGER) AS calendar_year,
         CAST(strftime('%m', date(min_month || '-01', '+' || (n||' months')) ) AS INTEGER) AS calendar_month,
         n AS month_index
  FROM (
    SELECT MIN(strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date)) AS min_month,
           MAX(strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date)) AS max_month,
           ( ( (CAST(strftime('%Y', MAX(txn_date)) AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', MIN(txn_date)) AS INTEGER)) * 12)
             + (CAST(strftime('%m', MAX(txn_date)) AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%m', MIN(txn_date)) AS INTEGER)) ) AS months_diff
    FROM customer_transactions
  ), 
  -- generate sequence 0..months_diff
  (SELECT 0 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9
   UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11 UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14 UNION ALL SELECT 15 UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17 UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19
   UNION ALL SELECT 20 UNION ALL SELECT 21 UNION ALL SELECT 22 UNION ALL SELECT 23 UNION ALL SELECT 24 UNION ALL SELECT 25 UNION ALL SELECT 26 UNION ALL SELECT 27 UNION ALL SELECT 28 UNION ALL SELECT 29
   UNION ALL SELECT 30 UNION ALL SELECT 31 UNION ALL SELECT 32 UNION ALL SELECT 33 UNION ALL SELECT 34 UNION ALL SELECT 35 UNION ALL SELECT 36) seq
  WHERE n <= months_diff
),
customers AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions
),
customer_months AS (
  -- cross join customers to full month grid so every customer has every month
  SELECT c.customer_id, m.month_start_date, m.calendar_year, m.calendar_month, m.month_index
  FROM customers c CROSS JOIN months m
),
monthly_agg AS (
  -- aggregate transactions per customer per calendar month
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', txn_date)) AS month_start_date,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS calendar_year,
    CAST(strftime('%m', txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS calendar_month,
    SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS total_deposits_amount,
    SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS total_withdrawals_amount,
    SUM(txn_amount) AS total_txn_amount,
    COUNT(*) AS txn_count
  FROM customer_transactions
  GROUP BY customer_id, calendar_year, calendar_month, month_start_date
),
customer_monthly AS (
  -- left join to ensure months with no activity are present with zeros
  SELECT
    cm.customer_id,
    cm.calendar_year,
    cm.calendar_month,
    cm.month_start_date,
    COALESCE(ma.total_deposits_amount, 0) AS month_total_deposits,
    COALESCE(ma.total_withdrawals_amount, 0) AS month_total_withdrawals,
    COALESCE(ma.total_txn_amount, 0) AS month_change,
    COALESCE(ma.txn_count, 0) AS month_txn_count,
    cm.month_index
  FROM customer_months cm
  LEFT JOIN monthly_agg ma
    ON ma.customer_id = cm.customer_id
   AND ma.month_start_date = cm.month_start_date
),
running AS (
  -- compute running (cumulative) balance per customer up to each month
  SELECT
    cm.customer_id,
    cm.calendar_year,
    cm.calendar_month,
    cm.month_start_date,
    cm.month_change,
    cm.month_txn_count,
    cm.month_total_deposits,
    cm.month_total_withdrawals,
    -- cumulative sum of month_change up to and including current month
    (SELECT SUM(cm2.month_change)
     FROM customer_monthly cm2
     WHERE cm2.customer_id = cm.customer_id
       AND (cm2.month_index <= cm.month_index)
    ) AS month_balance,
    -- cumulative sum up to previous month
    (SELECT SUM(cm3.month_change)
     FROM customer_monthly cm3
     WHERE cm3.customer_id = cm.customer_id
       AND (cm3.month_index < cm.month_index)
    ) AS prev_month_balance
  FROM customer_monthly cm
)
SELECT
  customer_id,
  calendar_year,
  calendar_month,
  month_start_date,
  month_change,
  month_txn_count,
  month_total_deposits,
  month_total_withdrawals,
  COALESCE(month_balance, 0) AS closing_balance,
  COALESCE(prev_month_balance, 0) AS prev_month_balance,
  COALESCE(month_balance, 0) - COALESCE(prev_month_balance, 0) AS month_over_month_change
FROM running
ORDER BY customer_id, calendar_year, calendar_month

rows.question: For each customer and each month of 2020, first calculate the month-end balance by adding all deposit amounts and subtracting all withdrawal amounts that occurred during that specific month. Then determine which month in 2020 has the highest count of customers with a positive month-end balance and which month has the lowest count. For each of these two months, compute the average month-end balance across all customers and provide the difference between these two averages

WITH all_customers_master_list AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id
  FROM (
    SELECT customer_id FROM customer_transactions
    UNION
    SELECT customer_id FROM customer_nodes
  )
),
customer_monthly_balances AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    -- normalize txn_date to YYYY-MM (handles YYYY-MM-DD; ignores malformed)
    CASE
      WHEN txn_date IS NULL THEN NULL
      WHEN length(txn_date) >= 7 AND substr(txn_date,5,1) = '-' THEN substr(txn_date,1,7)
      ELSE NULL
    END AS txn_month,
    LOWER(txn_type) AS txn_type,
    COALESCE(txn_amount,0) AS txn_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE txn_date BETWEEN '2020-01-01' AND '2020-12-31'
),
monthly AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_month,
    SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS sum_deposits,
    SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type <> 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS sum_withdrawals,
    SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END) AS month_balance
  FROM customer_monthly_balances
  WHERE txn_month IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id, txn_month
),
months AS (
  SELECT '2020-01' AS txn_month UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-02' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-03' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-04' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-05' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-06' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-07' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-08' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-09' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-10' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-11' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2020-12'
),
customer_month_grid AS (
  SELECT m.txn_month, c.customer_id,
         COALESCE(mm.month_balance, 0) AS month_balance
  FROM months m
  CROSS JOIN all_customers_master_list c
  LEFT JOIN monthly mm
    ON mm.customer_id = c.customer_id
   AND mm.txn_month = m.txn_month
),
month_stats AS (
  SELECT
    txn_month,
    SUM(CASE WHEN month_balance > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS positive_customer_count,
    AVG(month_balance) AS avg_balance
  FROM customer_month_grid
  GROUP BY txn_month
),
ranked_high AS (
  SELECT txn_month, positive_customer_count, avg_balance,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY positive_customer_count DESC, txn_month ASC) AS rn
  FROM month_stats
),
ranked_low AS (
  SELECT txn_month, positive_customer_count, avg_balance,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY positive_customer_count ASC, txn_month ASC) AS rn
  FROM month_stats
)
SELECT
  h.txn_month AS highest_month,
  h.positive_customer_count AS highest_month_positive_customer_count,
  h.avg_balance AS highest_month_avg_balance,
  l.txn_month AS lowest_month,
  l.positive_customer_count AS lowest_month_positive_customer_count,
  l.avg_balance AS lowest_month_avg_balance,
  (h.avg_balance - l.avg_balance) AS average_difference
FROM
  (SELECT txn_month, positive_customer_count, avg_balance FROM ranked_high WHERE rn = 1) h,
  (SELECT txn_month, positive_customer_count, avg_balance FROM ranked_low WHERE rn = 1) l
LIMIT 1

rows.question: For each customer, group all deposits and withdrawals by the first day of each month to obtain a monthly net amount, then calculate each month’s closing balance by cumulatively summing these monthly nets. Next, determine the most recent month’s growth rate by comparing its closing balance to the prior month’s balance, treating deposits as positive and withdrawals as negative, and if the previous month’s balance is zero, the growth rate should be the current month’s balance multiplied by 100. Finally, compute the percentage of customers whose most recent month shows a growth rate of more than 5%.

WITH customer_transactions_normalized AS (
  SELECT
    ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
    substr(ct.txn_date,1,10) AS txn_date,
    (substr(ct.txn_date,1,7) || '-01') AS txn_month_start,
    CASE WHEN lower(ct.txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount ELSE -ct.txn_amount END AS signed_txn_amount,
    CAST(substr(ct.txn_date,1,4) AS INTEGER) AS txn_year,
    CAST(substr(ct.txn_date,6,2) AS INTEGER) AS txn_month
  FROM customer_transactions ct
),
customer_monthly_nets AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_month_start,
    txn_year,
    txn_month,
    SUM(signed_txn_amount) AS monthly_net
  FROM customer_transactions_normalized
  GROUP BY customer_id, txn_month_start, txn_year, txn_month
),
customer_monthly_with_closing AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_month_start,
    txn_year,
    txn_month,
    monthly_net,
    SUM(monthly_net) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY txn_year, txn_month ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS closing_balance
  FROM customer_monthly_nets
),
customer_latest AS (
  SELECT
    cmw.customer_id,
    cmw.txn_month_start,
    cmw.closing_balance,
    LAG(cmw.closing_balance) OVER (PARTITION BY cmw.customer_id ORDER BY cmw.txn_year, cmw.txn_month) AS prior_closing_balance,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cmw.customer_id ORDER BY cmw.txn_year DESC, cmw.txn_month DESC) AS rn_desc
  FROM customer_monthly_with_closing cmw
)
SELECT
  100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN growth_rate > 0.05 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(customer_id), 0) AS percentage_customers_gt_5pct_growth
FROM (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    closing_balance,
    prior_closing_balance,
    CASE
      WHEN prior_closing_balance IS NULL OR prior_closing_balance = 0 THEN closing_balance * 100.0
      ELSE (closing_balance * 1.0 / prior_closing_balance) - 1.0
    END AS growth_rate
  FROM customer_latest
  WHERE rn_desc = 1
) t

WITH customer_transactions_clean AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_date AS txn_date_iso,
    txn_type,
    txn_amount,
    CASE
      WHEN txn_amount < 0 THEN txn_amount
      WHEN lower(trim(txn_type)) IN ('deposit','credit','topup','payment in') THEN abs(txn_amount)
      WHEN lower(trim(txn_type)) IN ('withdrawal','payment','debit','payout') THEN -abs(txn_amount)
      ELSE txn_amount
    END AS signed_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
    AND txn_date IS NOT NULL
    AND txn_amount IS NOT NULL
),
months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT substr(txn_date_iso,1,7) || '-01' AS month_start
  FROM customer_transactions_clean
),
earliest_month AS (
  SELECT min(month_start) AS month_start FROM months
),
customer_monthly_balance_snapshot AS (
  SELECT
    c.customer_id,
    m.month_start,
    COALESCE((
      SELECT SUM(ctc2.signed_amount)
      FROM customer_transactions_clean ctc2
      WHERE ctc2.customer_id = c.customer_id
        AND date(ctc2.txn_date_iso) < date(m.month_start)
    ),0) AS balance_as_of_month_start
  FROM
    (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions_clean) c
  CROSS JOIN
    months m
)
SELECT
  m.month_start AS month,
  SUM(CASE WHEN s.balance_as_of_month_start < 0 THEN 0 ELSE s.balance_as_of_month_start END) AS total_balance_previous_month_as_of_first_day
FROM months m
JOIN customer_monthly_balance_snapshot s
  ON m.month_start = s.month_start
LEFT JOIN earliest_month e
  ON m.month_start = e.month_start
WHERE e.month_start IS NULL
GROUP BY m.month_start
ORDER BY m.month_start ASC

    AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id

    AND er.over_id = b.over_id

rows.question: Which bowler has the lowest bowling average per wicket taken?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH delivery AS (
  SELECT
    b.match_id,
    b.innings_no,
    b.over_id,
    b.ball_id,
    b.bowler
  FROM ball_by_ball b
),
runs_and_extras AS (
  SELECT
    d.match_id,
    d.innings_no,
    d.over_id,
    d.ball_id,
    d.bowler,
    COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) AS runs_scored,
    COALESCE(e.extra_runs, 0) AS extra_runs
  FROM delivery d
  LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
    ON bs.match_id = d.match_id
    AND bs.innings_no = d.innings_no
    AND bs.over_id = d.over_id
    AND bs.ball_id = d.ball_id
  LEFT JOIN extra_runs e
    ON e.match_id = d.match_id
    AND e.innings_no = d.innings_no
    AND e.over_id = d.over_id
    AND e.ball_id = d.ball_id
),
bowler_stats AS (
  SELECT
    r.bowler AS bowler,
    SUM(r.runs_scored + r.extra_runs) AS total_runs_conceded,
    SUM(CASE WHEN w.player_out IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS total_wickets_taken
  FROM runs_and_extras r
  LEFT JOIN wicket_taken w
    ON w.match_id = r.match_id
    AND w.innings_no = r.innings_no
    AND w.over_id = r.over_id
    AND w.ball_id = r.ball_id
  GROUP BY r.bowler
)
SELECT
  b.bowler AS player_id,
  p.player_name,
  COALESCE(b.total_runs_conceded, 0) AS total_runs_conceded,
  b.total_wickets_taken,
  (COALESCE(b.total_runs_conceded,0) * 1.0) / b.total_wickets_taken AS bowling_average
FROM bowler_stats b
JOIN player p ON p.player_id = b.bowler
WHERE b.total_wickets_taken > 0
ORDER BY bowling_average ASC, b.total_wickets_taken DESC, b.bowler ASC
LIMIT 1

rows.question: Please help me find the names of top 5 players with the highest average runs per match in season 5, along with their batting averages.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH batsman_runs_per_ball AS (
  SELECT
    b.match_id,
    b.innings_no,
    b.over_id,
    b.ball_id,
    bb.striker AS player_id,
    b.runs_scored
  FROM batsman_scored b
  JOIN ball_by_ball bb
    ON b.match_id = bb.match_id
    AND b.innings_no = bb.innings_no
    AND b.over_id = bb.over_id
    AND b.ball_id = bb.ball_id
  -- rows without matching ball_by_ball (no striker) are excluded by the JOIN
),
runs_per_player_match AS (
  -- total runs credited to a player in a given match (summing per-ball runs)
  SELECT
    match_id,
    player_id,
    SUM(runs_scored) AS runs_in_match
  FROM batsman_runs_per_ball
  GROUP BY match_id, player_id
),
batsman_ball_events AS (
  SELECT match_id, striker AS player_id FROM ball_by_ball WHERE striker IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT match_id, non_striker AS player_id FROM ball_by_ball WHERE non_striker IS NOT NULL
),
player_participation_by_match AS (
  -- players who participated in a match either by appearing in ball events or listed in player_match
  SELECT DISTINCT match_id, player_id FROM (
    SELECT * FROM batsman_ball_events
    UNION
    SELECT match_id, player_id FROM player_match
  )
),
season5_matches AS (
  SELECT match_id FROM "match" WHERE season_id = 5
),
season5_participation AS (
  -- restrict participation to season 5 matches
  SELECT ppm.match_id, ppm.player_id
  FROM player_participation_by_match ppm
  JOIN season5_matches s5 ON ppm.match_id = s5.match_id
),
player_season_stats AS (
  SELECT
    sp.player_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT sp.match_id) AS matches_played,
    COALESCE(SUM(rpm.runs_in_match), 0) AS total_runs

  LEFT JOIN runs_per_player_match rpm
    ON rpm.match_id = sp.match_id
    AND rpm.player_id = sp.player_id
  GROUP BY sp.player_id
)
SELECT
  pl.player_name,
  CAST(pss.total_runs AS REAL) / pss.matches_played AS batting_average
FROM player_season_stats pss

rows.question: Please examine our database records for Chinese cities (country_code_2 = 'cn') during July 2021 and identify both the shortest and longest streaks of consecutive date entries. For each date in these streaks, return exactly one record per date along with the corresponding city name. In your output, please ensure the first letter of each city name is capitalized and the rest are lowercase. Display the dates and city names for both the shortest and longest consecutive date streaks, ordered by date.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH cities_cn AS (
  SELECT
    city_id,
    CASE
      WHEN city_name IS NULL THEN NULL
      WHEN length(city_name) = 0 THEN city_name
      ELSE upper(substr(city_name,1,1)) || lower(substr(city_name,2))
    END AS city_name_normalized,
    country_code_2,
    insert_date
  FROM cities
  WHERE country_code_2 = 'cn'
    AND insert_date BETWEEN '2021-07-01' AND '2021-07-31'
    AND insert_date IS NOT NULL
),
-- one deterministic representative city per date: alphabetically first normalized name
daily_city AS (
  SELECT
    insert_date AS date,
    MIN(city_name_normalized) AS city_name
  FROM cities_cn
  GROUP BY insert_date
),
-- identify streak groups by date difference trick
streaks AS (
  SELECT
    date,
    city_name,
    julianday(date) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY date) AS grp
  FROM daily_city
),
streak_ranges AS (
  SELECT
    grp,
    MIN(date) AS streak_start,
    MAX(date) AS streak_end,
    CAST(julianday(MAX(date)) - julianday(MIN(date)) + 1 AS INTEGER) AS streak_length
  FROM streaks
  GROUP BY grp
),
minmax AS (
  SELECT MIN(streak_length) AS min_len, MAX(streak_length) AS max_len FROM streak_ranges
),
wanted_streaks AS (
  SELECT sr.* FROM streak_ranges sr, minmax m
  WHERE sr.streak_length IN (m.min_len, m.max_len)
)
SELECT
  s.date AS date,
  s.city_name AS city_name,
  CASE WHEN wr.streak_length = (SELECT min_len FROM minmax) THEN 'shortest' ELSE 'longest' END AS streak_type
FROM streaks s
JOIN wanted_streaks wr ON s.grp = wr.grp
ORDER BY
  CASE WHEN wr.streak_length = (SELECT min_len FROM minmax) THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
  s.date

rows.question: Could you review our records in June 2022 and identify which countries have the longest streak of consecutive inserted city dates? Please list the 2-letter length country codes of these countries.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH june_rows AS (
  SELECT
    country_code_2,
    DATE(substr(insert_date,1,10)) AS date
  FROM cities
  WHERE insert_date IS NOT NULL
    AND TRIM(country_code_2) != ''
    AND country_code_2 IS NOT NULL
    AND DATE(substr(insert_date,1,10)) BETWEEN '2022-06-01' AND '2022-06-30'
),
country_dates AS (
  -- one row per country + date (deduplicate multiple inserts same day)
  SELECT country_code_2, date
  FROM june_rows
  GROUP BY country_code_2, date
),
dated_groups AS (
  -- assign a group key by subtracting row_number days from the date; consecutive dates will share the same key
  SELECT
    country_code_2,
    date,
    DATE(date, printf('-%d days', ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY country_code_2 ORDER BY date))) AS grp_key
  FROM country_dates
),
runs AS (
  -- compute run lengths per country per group
  SELECT country_code_2,
         COUNT(*) AS run_length
  FROM dated_groups
  GROUP BY country_code_2, grp_key
),
country_max AS (
  -- maximum run per country
  SELECT country_code_2,
         MAX(run_length) AS country_max_streak
  FROM runs
  GROUP BY country_code_2
),
overall_max AS (
  SELECT MAX(country_max_streak) AS max_streak FROM country_max
)
-- return countries that tie for the global maximum streak and the streak length
SELECT c.country_code_2, c.country_max_streak AS max_streak
FROM country_max c
JOIN overall_max o ON c.country_max_streak = o.max_streak

rows.question: Identify the country with data inserted on nine different days in January 2022. Then, find the longest consecutive period with data insertions for this country during January 2022, and calculate the proportion of entries that are from its capital city within this longest consecutive insertion period.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH cities_countries_jan AS (
  -- consider only rows in January 2022 using created_on
  SELECT
    country_id,
    country_name,
    country_code_2,
    created_on AS insert_date
  FROM cities_countries
  WHERE created_on BETWEEN '2022-01-01' AND '2022-01-31'
),
country_with_nine_days AS (
  -- country with exactly 9 distinct insert days in Jan 2022
  SELECT
    country_name,
    country_code_2
  FROM cities_countries_jan
  GROUP BY country_name, country_code_2
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT insert_date) = 9
  LIMIT 1
),
distinct_dates AS (
  -- distinct dates for that country, ordered
  SELECT DISTINCT insert_date
  FROM cities_countries_jan
  WHERE country_code_2 = (SELECT country_code_2 FROM country_with_nine_days)
  ORDER BY insert_date
),
date_groups AS (
  -- assign group by shifting dates by row number to identify consecutive runs
  SELECT
    insert_date,
    DATE(insert_date, '-' || (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY insert_date) - 1) || ' days') AS grp
  FROM distinct_dates
),
sequences AS (
  SELECT
    MIN(insert_date) AS start_date,
    MAX(insert_date) AS end_date,
    CAST((julianday(MAX(insert_date)) - julianday(MIN(insert_date))) + 1 AS INTEGER) AS sequence_length_days
  FROM date_groups
  GROUP BY grp
),
longest_sequence AS (
  SELECT start_date, end_date, sequence_length_days
  FROM sequences
  ORDER BY sequence_length_days DESC, start_date ASC
  LIMIT 1
),
seq_row_counts AS (
  -- count cities_countries rows for the country within the longest sequence period
  SELECT
    cc.country_code_2,
    COUNT(*) AS total_rows_in_sequence
  FROM cities_countries cc
  WHERE cc.created_on BETWEEN (SELECT start_date FROM longest_sequence) AND (SELECT end_date FROM longest_sequence)
    AND cc.country_code_2 = (SELECT country_code_2 FROM country_with_nine_days)
  GROUP BY cc.country_code_2
),
seq_capital_counts AS (
  -- count how many of those rows correspond to capital cities by joining on country_code_2 to cities;
  -- a cities_countries row counts as capital if any cities row for that country_code_2 has capital = 1.
  SELECT
    cc.country_code_2,
    SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM cities c
      WHERE c.country_code_2 = cc.country_code_2
        AND c.capital = 1
    ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS capital_rows_in_sequence
  FROM cities_countries cc
  WHERE cc.created_on BETWEEN (SELECT start_date FROM longest_sequence) AND (SELECT end_date FROM longest_sequence)
    AND cc.country_code_2 = (SELECT country_code_2 FROM country_with_nine_days)
  GROUP BY cc.country_code_2
)
SELECT
  cwn.country_name,
  cwn.country_code_2,
  (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT insert_date) FROM cities_countries_jan WHERE country_code_2 = cwn.country_code_2) AS distinct_insert_days_in_jan_2022,
  (SELECT start_date FROM longest_sequence) AS longest_sequence_start_date,
  (SELECT end_date FROM longest_sequence) AS longest_sequence_end_date,
  (SELECT sequence_length_days FROM longest_sequence) AS sequence_length_days,
  COALESCE(src.total_rows_in_sequence, 0) AS total_rows_in_sequence,
  COALESCE(scc.capital_rows_in_sequence, 0) AS capital_rows_in_sequence,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(src.total_rows_in_sequence, 0) = 0 THEN 0.0
       ELSE CAST(COALESCE(scc.capital_rows_in_sequence, 0) AS REAL) / src.total_rows_in_sequence END AS capital_proportion
FROM country_with_nine_days cwn
LEFT JOIN seq_row_counts src ON src.country_code_2 = cwn.country_code_2
LEFT JOIN seq_capital_counts scc ON scc.country_code_2 = cwn.country_code_2
LIMIT 1

rows.question: Calculate the number of new cities inserted in April, May, and June for each year from 2021 to 2023. For each month, compute the cumulative running total of cities added for that specific month across the years up to and including the given year (i.e., sum the counts of that month over the years). Additionally, calculate the year-over-year growth percentages for both the monthly total and the running total for each month, comparing each year to the previous year. Present the results only for 2022 and 2023, listing the year, the month, the total number of cities added in that month, the cumulative running total for that month, and the year-over-year growth percentages for both the monthly total and the running total. Use the data from 2021 solely as a baseline for calculating growth rates, and exclude it from the final output.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH parsed AS (
  SELECT
    city_id,
    insert_date,
    CAST(substr(insert_date,1,4) AS INTEGER) AS yr,
    CAST(substr(insert_date,6,2) AS INTEGER) AS mon,
    CASE CAST(substr(insert_date,6,2) AS INTEGER)
      WHEN 4 THEN 'April' WHEN 5 THEN 'May' WHEN 6 THEN 'June'
      WHEN 1 THEN 'January' WHEN 2 THEN 'February' WHEN 3 THEN 'March'
      WHEN 7 THEN 'July' WHEN 8 THEN 'August' WHEN 9 THEN 'September'
      WHEN 10 THEN 'October' WHEN 11 THEN 'November' WHEN 12 THEN 'December'
    END AS mon_name
  FROM cities
  WHERE insert_date IS NOT NULL
),
monthly_counts AS (
  -- counts for years 2021-2023 and months 4-6 (we keep 2021 as baseline)
  SELECT
    yr AS insert_year,
    mon AS insert_month,
    mon_name AS insert_month_name,
    COUNT(*) AS month_total
  FROM parsed
  WHERE yr IN (2021,2022,2023)
    AND mon IN (4,5,6)
  GROUP BY yr, mon, mon_name
),
-- ensure rows exist for combinations that may be missing by generating all combos and left joining counts
months AS (
  SELECT 4 AS mon, 'April' AS mon_name UNION ALL
  SELECT 5, 'May' UNION ALL
  SELECT 6, 'June'
),
years AS (
  SELECT 2021 AS yr UNION ALL SELECT 2022 UNION ALL SELECT 2023
),
all_combos AS (
  SELECT y.yr AS insert_year, m.mon AS insert_month, m.mon_name AS insert_month_name
  FROM years y CROSS JOIN months m
),
monthly_counts_filled AS (
  SELECT
    ac.insert_year,
    ac.insert_month,
    ac.insert_month_name,
    COALESCE(mc.month_total, 0) AS month_total
  FROM all_combos ac
  LEFT JOIN monthly_counts mc
    ON ac.insert_year = mc.insert_year
   AND ac.insert_month = mc.insert_month
),
running_totals AS (
  -- running total for each month across years up to that year (including 2021 baseline)
  SELECT
    mcf.insert_year,
    mcf.insert_month,
    mcf.insert_month_name,
    mcf.month_total,
    (SELECT SUM(month_total)
     FROM monthly_counts_filled sub
     WHERE sub.insert_month = mcf.insert_month
       AND sub.insert_year <= mcf.insert_year
    ) AS running_total
  FROM monthly_counts_filled mcf
)
SELECT
  cur.insert_year AS year,
  cur.insert_month_name AS month,
  cur.month_total,
  cur.running_total,
  CASE
    WHEN prior.month_total IS NULL OR prior.month_total = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE ((cur.month_total - prior.month_total) * 1.0 / prior.month_total) * 100.0
  END AS monthly_yoy_growth_pct,
  CASE
    WHEN prior.running_total IS NULL OR prior.running_total = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE ((cur.running_total - prior.running_total) * 1.0 / prior.running_total) * 100.0
  END AS running_yoy_growth_pct
FROM running_totals cur
LEFT JOIN running_totals prior
  ON cur.insert_month = prior.insert_month
 AND cur.insert_year = prior.insert_year + 1
WHERE cur.insert_year IN (2022,2023)
ORDER BY
  cur.insert_year ASC,
  CASE cur.insert_month_name WHEN 'April' THEN 4 WHEN 'May' THEN 5 WHEN 'June' THEN 6 END ASC
